introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0796 INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGIES 1, ADVANCED LEVEL, JUNE 2024. Multiple choice question paper. Duration: one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Use a soft HB pencil. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Electronic calculators are not allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question (if more than one answer is marked, the question scores zero). Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Do all rough work in the question booklet.

Réponse visée dans chaque corrigé.

questions.enonce_markdown: The size of the monitor is determined by the ...... of the monitor.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The size of a monitor (for example 15.6 inches or 21 inches) is always quoted as the **diagonal** of the visible screen, measured from one corner to the opposite corner. Height and width alone, or their sum, are never used as the nominal size.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following does not influence the processing ability of a computer?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The processing ability (speed at which instructions are handled) depends on the processor clock speed and the components that feed it with data: the **bus width** (how many bits move at once), the **cache memory** (fast memory close to the CPU) and the **RAM** (working memory). The size of the local (hard) disk only gives storage capacity: a bigger disk stores more files but does not make the processor work faster.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A professional who gives advice on the set up of computers in a room is a/an
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **ergonomist** studies how people work with equipment and advises on the layout of the room, the position of the screen, the chair, the desk and the lighting so that users avoid fatigue and injuries. A database administrator manages data, a maintenance technician repairs hardware and a system analyst studies and designs information systems.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A system that can track the movement of animals in a forest area is
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **geographic information system (GIS)**, usually combined with GPS tags or collars, captures, stores and displays data linked to geographic positions, so the movement of animals can be tracked on a map. A knowledge based (expert) system gives advice from rules and a control system regulates a process through sensors and actuators; neither maps positions.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The security measure that converts information to unreadable form is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Encryption** scrambles data (plaintext) into an unreadable form (ciphertext) using an algorithm and a key, so that only a person holding the key can read it. Deciphering is the reverse operation (making it readable again), bugging means secretly listening or installing a device, and coding is a general word for writing a program or assigning codes.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The i7 laptop that is mostly used today by students is classified as ...... computer.

*Options as printed:* A) 5th generation   B) 4th generation   C) 3rd generation   D) 2nd generation
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the classical classification of computer generations, the first used vacuum tubes, the second transistors, the third integrated circuits and the **fourth microprocessors**. Personal computers and laptops built around a microprocessor such as the Intel Core i7 belong to the fourth generation; the fifth generation refers to artificial intelligence and parallel processing machines that are still a research target.

**Intended answer: B (4th generation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: An office door that is opened through eye scan is said to use
questions.corrige_markdown:
Identifying a person by a unique body feature (eye iris or retina, fingerprint, face, voice) is **biometrics**. A CT scan is a medical imaging technique, and an automatic system or artificial intelligence do not necessarily identify a person from a body feature.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The act of modifying data from a remote position without authorization is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Hacking** is gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or network, often from a remote place, in order to view, change or destroy data. Phishing tricks people into giving their details through fake messages, scamming is fraud and network logging simply records network activity.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following does not imply the presence of a virus in a computer?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Typical signs of a virus are a computer that suddenly becomes slow, strange behaviour caused by the virus itself (pop-ups, files deleted or copied, programs opening alone) and files whose extension has changed or doubled (for example .jpg.exe). The mere presence of some **special software** on a machine is not a sign of infection (it may well be an anti-virus or a normal tool).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Computer performance can be improved by:

*Options as printed:* A) defragmentation   B) file deletion   C) hard disk upgrade   D) ROM upgrade
questions.corrige_markdown:
Defragmentation regroups the pieces of files scattered on the disk, so the read head moves less and files open faster. Upgrading the hard disk (for example to a faster SSD) can also speed a computer up, so two printed options are defensible. Deleting files only frees space and ROM holds fixed start-up instructions and is not normally upgraded.

**Intended answer: A (defragmentation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The probable need for a computer that cannot output sound is

*Options as printed:* A) encoder   B) volume   C) players   D) drivers
questions.corrige_markdown:
A computer that cannot produce sound has most probably lost, or never had, the software that lets the operating system talk to the sound card and the speakers: the **device (audio) drivers**. An encoder converts data to a format and a player plays media files; "volume" (the sound being muted or turned down) is also a plausible first thing to check, and the sentence itself is vague.

**Intended answer: D (drivers).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The quality of images in the computer can be improved by
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **graphics (video) card** processes the picture and decides the resolution and colour depth sent to the screen, so a better card improves image quality. A larger monitor only makes the same image bigger, brightness changes lighting and more RAM improves general speed rather than image quality.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The network in which signals are made to move in one direction is the
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a **ring** network each node is connected to exactly two neighbours and the data (or the token) circulates around the ring in a single direction. A bus carries signals in both directions along the cable, a mesh has several possible paths, and round robin is a scheduling technique, not a topology.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The unit in a CPU that performs binary operations is
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **arithmetic and logic unit (ALU)** carries out arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, ...) and logical operations (AND, OR, NOT, comparisons) on binary data. The accumulator only stores intermediate results and the control unit directs the operations without computing.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Signal interference in data transmission is reduced by
questions.corrige_markdown:
Twisting the two wires of a pair (as in twisted pair cables) makes the interference picked up by each wire cancel out, which reduces crosstalk and noise. Burying a cable protects it from weather, not from interference, the number of ports is irrelevant and coaxial cable is not the only shielded medium.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: burying of cable on the ground

questions.enonce_markdown: The amount of data that flows in a network medium at a given time is defined by the
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Bandwidth** is the amount of data that can be carried through a transmission medium in a given time, measured in bits per second (kbps, Mbps, Gbps). A switch, a server and a cable are devices or media, not a measure.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Systems that collect data over a period of time before processing is done are known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **batch processing** the transactions are gathered into a batch over a period (a day, a week, a month) and then processed together, as in payroll or bills. Time sharing lets many users share the CPU in turn, and the other two names are not processing modes.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The organization of files in the local storage of a computer is carried out by the
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **file manager** is the part of the operating system that creates, names, moves, copies and deletes files and folders and keeps track of where they are stored on the disk. The CPU only executes instructions; Windows Explorer is one particular file manager and the operating system is the wider set of programs, so the most precise printed option is the file manager. Option A is also defensible, which is why the key is noted as uncertain.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A DBMS is classified as a/an

*Options as printed:* A) specialised software   B) generic software   C) system software   D) application software
questions.corrige_markdown:
A database management system such as Microsoft Access or MySQL is general purpose software that can be used for many different data tasks, which is called **generic application software** (like word processors and spreadsheets). Specialised software is written for one job (payroll, school management), and system software controls the hardware. Option D is true in a wider sense since generic software is a kind of application software.

**Intended answer: B (generic software).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Instructions from the local storage get to the central processing unit through the
questions.corrige_markdown:
A program stored on the disk (local storage) is first loaded into **random access memory (RAM)**, and the CPU fetches each instruction from RAM. The CPU does not read directly from the disk because the disk is far too slow. Registers sit inside the CPU, so they receive instructions after RAM, not before.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following text editor is suitable for programming?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A program source file must be saved as plain text without formatting, which is what a text editor such as **Notepad** does. Firefox is a browser and MS Word is a word processor that adds hidden formatting codes. Pelles C is a C compiler and development environment rather than a simple text editor, so the key is noted as uncertain.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A programming language structured data type whose items can be accessed by an index.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **array** is a structured data type that stores a fixed number of items of the same type, each reached by its position (index), for example `marks[3]`. In a record the fields are reached by name, a file is read sequentially or by record number, and a set has no ordering.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A feature in e-mail accounts that keeps unwanted mails coming from particular persons is
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **filter** (rule) is set in the mailbox to block or move to another folder the messages coming from chosen senders. Spam is the unwanted mail itself, cookies are small files stored by a browser and a mailer daemon is the automatic message reporting a delivery failure.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A development strategy in which the final product is constructed from a model is
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **prototyping** a working model (prototype) is built first, shown to the users and improved until it satisfies them; the final system is then constructed from that model. The SDLC is the whole life cycle of a system, and modelling and simulation represent behaviour but are not development strategies.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The steps on how to solve a problem are clearly stated. This programming paradigm is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the **imperative paradigm** the programmer writes, step by step, the sequence of instructions that tells the computer *how* to solve the problem (Pascal and C are imperative). In the declarative paradigm the programmer states *what* result is wanted, and the functional and object-oriented paradigms are organised around functions and objects.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A technique that results to independent sub programs that can work together to solve a problem is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Modular programming** divides a program into independent modules (subprograms, functions, procedures) that are written and tested separately and then work together. Stepwise refinement and the top-down approach are ways of breaking a problem down, and the bottom-up approach builds from small parts upwards; the result of the modular technique is the independent subprograms.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A typical encryption algorithm makes use of
questions.corrige_markdown:
Encryption algorithms and the protocols built on them rely on mathematical functions that turn data into an unreadable form, and the best known family is that of **hash and cipher functions** (hashing is used in digital signatures and integrity checks). "Cryptic functions" is not a technical term, and recursion and iteration are programming techniques, not encryption methods. The printed question is vague, so the key is noted as uncertain.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The network configuration is done at the

*Options as printed:* A) server   B) switch   C) backbone   D) router.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Configuring a network (addresses, routes, security rules) is mainly done on the **router**, the device that connects networks and must be told how to forward packets. A server can also hold part of the configuration (for example a DHCP service) and a switch is usually plug and play, so the printed options are not reliable enough to be marked automatically.

**Intended answer: D (router).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The function of a modem is to

*Options as printed:* A) select transmission path   B) increase transmission speed   C) inter connect devices   D) reduce interference
questions.corrige_markdown:
A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts the digital signals of a computer into analogue signals that can travel on a telephone line or cable, and converts the incoming analogue signals back to digital form. It thereby connects a computer to a communication line. None of the printed options states this exactly: selecting the path is the job of a router, and increasing speed or reducing interference are not functions of a modem; "inter connect devices" is the closest.

**Intended answer: C (inter connect devices).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Transmitted data in a network is secured by
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Encryption** makes the data unreadable to anyone who intercepts it during transmission. Binary coding only represents data in 0s and 1s, compression reduces the file size and masquerading means pretending to be another user, which is an attack.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The abstract data type that is defined by the head and a tail is the
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **list** is described recursively as a head (its first element) followed by a tail (the rest of the list, itself a list), as in list processing languages such as Lisp and Prolog. A stack is defined by its top (LIFO), a queue by its front and rear (FIFO), and a binary tree by a root with left and right subtrees.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A sign showing that the printer is effectively connected to a computer is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Handshaking** is the exchange of control signals between the computer and a peripheral (ready, busy, acknowledge) that shows the two devices are connected and able to communicate. Buffering is temporary storage of data, polling is the CPU checking devices in turn and an interrupt is a signal asking for the CPU's attention.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Internet stores information in
questions.corrige_markdown:
Web pages, e-mails and files on the Internet are kept on **servers** (computers permanently connected to the network, which of course use hard disks inside). Routers only forward data, and the atmosphere stores nothing.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The best cable transmission medium for broadband communication is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Fibre optic cable** carries light signals, giving the highest bandwidth, the lowest attenuation over long distances and immunity to electromagnetic interference, so it is the best medium for broadband. Coaxial and twisted pair cables have a lower bandwidth and are more sensitive to noise.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The physical layout on how devices are connected in a network is called
questions.corrige_markdown:
The way the devices (nodes) and cables are arranged in a network (bus, star, ring, mesh, tree) is the **network topology**. Configuration refers to the settings of the devices, not their layout.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An HTML script can be displayed to the user with the help of
questions.corrige_markdown:
An HTML file is a document written with tags; a **web browser** (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) reads the tags and displays the formatted page. HTML is not compiled or assembled, and an interpreter runs programming language statements rather than displaying a page.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A network cable is connected to a computer through
questions.corrige_markdown:
A network (Ethernet) cable ends with an RJ45 plug that fits into the **RJ45 interface** (port) of the network card. The motherboard holds the card but is not the connector, the ethernet cable is the cable itself, and a PS/2 port is for a keyboard or a mouse. ("Interphase" is printed in the paper instead of "interface".)

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The role of a gateway in a network is to
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **gateway** is the entry and exit point between two different networks (for example a LAN and the Internet); it controls the traffic passing between them and translates protocols when they differ. Choosing the best path for packets is the router's role, boosting signals is the repeater's and sending data only to the requesting computer is what a switch does.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: selects the best path for network packets
boosts the strength of signals to cover long distances
receive and sends signals only to requesting computers in a network

questions.enonce_markdown:
In HTML, the tags
    ----
are used to
questions.corrige_markdown:
`<ul>` means *unordered list*: the items written with `<li>` are shown with bullets. A numbered list uses `<ol>` and text is underlined with `<u>`.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If the 1st character in the ASCII code is 00000001, then the code of the 74th character is
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first character has code 1, so the $n$-th character has code $n$. The 74th character therefore has code 74.

$74 = 64 + 8 + 2 = 2^6 + 2^3 + 2^1$, so in 8 bits: $74 = 0100\ 1010$ (a check by script gives `01001010`).

The other options are 146 (1001 0010), 38 (0010 0110) and 194 (1100 0010). The trap is to count the 74th character as code 73 or to read 1001 0010, which is 146.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The meaning of instructions in the machine cycle can be derived at the ...... phase?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the machine (fetch-decode-execute) cycle, the instruction is first fetched from memory, then the control unit **decodes** it, that is, works out its meaning (which operation and which operands), and finally it is executed.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a good characteristic of an algorithm?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A good algorithm must be executable, unambiguous (each step clear), **definite** (precise) and finite (it has a beginning and an end). "Indefinite" is the opposite of definite, so it is the characteristic that an algorithm must NOT have.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It must have a beginning and end

questions.enonce_markdown: The function defined as F(n)=F(n-1)+F(1) is described in programming as
questions.corrige_markdown:
The function $F(n)$ is defined in terms of itself ($F(n-1)$ appears on the right-hand side), which is the definition of **recursion**. A loop repeats instructions without the subprogram calling itself, and a routine or procedure is simply a named subprogram.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A code that cannot be modified by the programmer that is only executable by the machine is
questions.corrige_markdown:
The compiler translates the source code into **object code** (machine code in binary), which only the machine can execute and which a programmer cannot sensibly edit. Source code not yet compiled can be modified, pseudocode is only a human description of an algorithm and an error code reports a fault.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is a specific advantage of object-oriented programming?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Object-oriented programming builds programs from classes and objects, which can be **reused** (inheritance and composition) in other programs, saving development time. Security and portability are not specific to it, and object-oriented programs are generally not faster.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The series of tasks that gives the shortest time that the project can be completed is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
In project management (CPM, PERT), the **critical path** is the sequence of dependent tasks that fixes the minimum time needed to complete the project: any delay on it delays the whole project. It is the longest path through the network of tasks, which is what gives the shortest possible overall duration. The other terms are not standard.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an activity in the design phase of SDLC?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the design phase the analyst specifies the new system (inputs, outputs, files, screens, processing) and prepares the **test plan and test data** that will be used later. Finding the weaknesses of the old system belongs to analysis, writing code to implementation (coding) and testing the system to the testing phase. Some textbooks place test data in the testing phase, so the key is noted as uncertain.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Find the weakness of the system

questions.enonce_markdown: One cause of repetitive stress injury is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Repetitive strain (stress) injury, such as carpal tunnel syndrome, comes from repeating the same movement many times without rest, like **typing for a long period** or using the mouse. LCD monitors are not harmful in this way, and long eye contact with a screen causes eye strain, not repetitive stress injury. ("Bad tables" is printed as such; a badly adjusted desk can contribute but is not the direct cause.)

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: long eye contact with the monitor

questions.enonce_markdown: The system that is used to manage database is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **database management system (DBMS)** is the software used to create, store, query, update and secure a database. A relational database is the data organised in related tables, SQL is the language used to query it, and a data sheet is only a table view.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: To avoid redundancy in a large database,
questions.corrige_markdown:
Redundancy (the same data stored several times) is reduced by **normalisation**: the data is split into several related tables (linked by keys) so each fact is stored once. Using a single table repeats data in every row, deleting the repeated data is a cure after the fact and not a design method, and limiting a table to 5 fields has no connection with redundancy.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: use many tables to store data
use tables with not more than 5 fields
